study_identification_part.si4_title: Brain-Charting Autism and Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder Reveals Distinct and Overlapping Neurobiology

cm1_research_objectives.reason: The introduction explicitly states that the study leverages previously developed models of average brain development to quantify alterations related to autism and ADHD, investigates sex- and age-related variability, and examines co-occurring autism+ADHD, which covers both the research questions and the purpose of applying normative modeling.
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: Here, we leveraged models of average brain development previously characterized by our group (98) to quantify alterations related to autism and ADHD... We examined sources of variability related to sex, age, and measures of autistic and ADHD traits. Finally, we examined whether a subset of individuals with cooccurring autism and ADHD presented with distinct alterations.

nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.reason: The paper uses an existing BrainCharts normative model and cites the original publication with the reference cohort size (75,241 typically developing individuals) but does not detail inclusion/exclusion or quality standards or exclusions for that reference cohort in this article.
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.supporting_text: Our previous work (98) generated reference models... using a sample of 75,241 TD individuals... while accounting for effects of age, sex, and site/scanner.

nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.reason: The reference models account for age, sex, and site/scanner effects, and ComBat harmonization for this study used age, sex, and diagnosis as covariates to handle site effects before applying the normative model.
nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.supporting_text: Sex-specific life span developmental trajectories... were estimated... accounting for site- and scanner-specific variables (98). ComBat was applied... with covariates of age, sex, and diagnosis to preserve related biological variation.

nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.reason: The reference cohort is described as 75,241 typically developing individuals from prior work (BrainCharts) and the prior publication is cited, but this article does not enumerate the individual datasets or collection period for that reference cohort.
nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.supporting_text: Our previous work (98) generated reference models... using a sample of 75,241 TD individuals... accounting for effects of age, sex, and site/scanner.

nm4_image_acquisition_protocol.reason: The study relies on existing multi-site datasets and an existing normative model rather than collecting primary imaging for the reference cohort; acquisition protocols for the reference are not applicable per the guidance for secondary data.
nm4_image_acquisition_protocol.supporting_text: T1-weighted scans were combined from 49 sites across 7 datasets... The final dataset after quality control (QC) included 4255 individuals...

nm5_data_preprocessing.reason: Preprocessing steps are described: all T1 images were processed with FreeSurfer v6.0.1 using the Desikan-Killiany atlas; scans underwent manual QC with FSQC and an Euler number covariate to account for residual quality effects.
nm5_data_preprocessing.supporting_text: T1 images from each dataset were processed using FreeSurfer, version 6.0.1... Regional estimates... extracted based on the Desikan-Killiany atlas... All scans underwent manual QC... using our FSQC tool... A cutoff of 2.5 was used for FSQC... we also included the FreeSurfer-derived Euler number... as a covariate.

nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: Our previous work (98) generated reference models... Out-of-sample centile scores for our study sample were generated based on these reference models...

nm11_reproducibility.supporting_text: Our previous work (98) generated reference models... Software; Algorithm | Brain Charts algorithm | https://github.com/ucam-department-of-psychiatry/Lifespan. T1 images were processed using FreeSurfer, version 6.0.1 (105).

cr1_selection_criteria_clinical_cohort.reason: Eligibility is described in broad terms (individuals with MRI data and primary autism or ADHD diagnoses or controls) and QC thresholds were applied, but detailed diagnostic criteria and exclusion reasons are not provided.
cr1_selection_criteria_clinical_cohort.supporting_text: Individuals with magnetic resonance imaging data and a primary diagnosis of autism or ADHD or no diagnosis were included... The final dataset after quality control (QC) included 4255 individuals... All scans underwent manual QC using our FSQC tool. A cutoff of 2.5 was used for FSQC.

cr2_handling_of_clinical_covariates.reason: Analyses included age, sex, and image-quality covariates, but no clinical covariates such as medication status, illness duration, or symptom severity were incorporated in the main models.
cr2_handling_of_clinical_covariates.supporting_text: All analyses included Euler number as a covariate, as well as age.

cr3_data_sources_clinical_cohort.reason: The clinical cohorts came from seven named datasets (ABIDE, POND, HBN, ADHD200, Female ASD, UK MRC-AIMS, UCSD Biomarkers of Autism), satisfying the requirement to specify data sources.
cr3_data_sources_clinical_cohort.supporting_text: T1-weighted scans were combined from 49 sites across 7 datasets, including the ABIDE, POND, HBN, ADHD200, Multimodal Developmental Neurogenetics of Females with ASD, UK MRC-AIMS, and the University of California San Diego Biomarkers of Autism study.

cr4_clinical_characteristics_clinical_co.reason: Sample sizes, sex breakdowns, and age range for each diagnostic group are reported, providing demographic characteristics of the clinical and control cohorts.
cr4_clinical_characteristics_clinical_co.supporting_text: The final dataset after quality control (QC) included 4255 individuals (1869 typically developing control participants [687 female, 1182 male], 987 individuals with ADHD [270 female, 717 male], and 1399 autistic individuals [288 female, 1111 male], ages 2-64 years [mean 14.0, median 12.4]).

cr5_clinical_assessment_measures.reason: Supplementary methods detail the clinical instruments used, including ADOS calibrated severity scores, Social Responsiveness Scale (SRS), Restricted Behaviour Scale Revised, and SWAN ADHD scales, along with brief descriptions of each measure.
cr5_clinical_assessment_measures.supporting_text: ADOS is the gold standard instrument for diagnosing autism; calibrated severity scores can be calculated. The Social Responsiveness Scale (SRS) is a 65 item self- or parent-report measure. The Strengths and Weaknesses of Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity-symptoms and Normal-behaviours (SWAN) is an 18-item parent report measure.

cr6_interpretation_of_deviation_scores.reason: The paper explains the centile scores' direction (0–1 with 0.5 as average) and uses quantitative thresholds for extreme deviation (top/bottom 1% centiles), but it does not provide detailed clinical interpretation of score magnitudes or explicit clinical cut-points.
cr6_interpretation_of_deviation_scores.supporting_text: Centile scores quantify variation in brain development and range from 0 to 1, with 0.5 representing the average of the reference sample. We first identified individuals who had centile scores in the top or bottom percentile; i.e. a centile score of >0.99, or <0.01 for each cortical region.
